p: brethren: He adds now consequently according to his manner, various admonitions: the first of them is, that they pray for the increase and passage of the Gospel, and for the safety of the faithful ministers of it.
unreasonable and wicked men: Who do not do or care about their duty.

for all men have not faith: It is no wonder that the Gospel is hated by so many, seeing that faith is a rare gift of God. Nonetheless, the Church will never be destroyed by the multitude of the wicked, because it is grounded and stayed upon the faithful promise of God.
evil: From Satan's snares, or from evil.
And we have confidence in the: The second admonition is, that they always follow the doctrine of the apostles as a rule for their life.

And the Lord direct your hearts: Thirdly, he diligently and earnestly admonishes them of two things which are given to us only by the grace of God, that is, of charity, and a watchful mind to the coming of Christ.
Now we command you: Fourthly, he says that idle and lazy persons ought not to be supported by the Church; indeed, they are not to be endured.

For yourselves know how ye ought: Lest he might seem to deal harshly with them, he sets forth himself as an example, who besides his travail in preaching, laboured with his hands, which he says he was not bound to do.

neither should he eat: What will we do then with those fat lazy monks, and sacrificing priests? A monk (says Socrates, book eight, of his Tripartite History) who does not work with hands, is like a thief.

you disorderly: How great a fault idleness is, he declares in that God created no man in vain or to no purpose, neither is there any to whom he has not allotted as it were a certain position and place. From which it follows, that the order which God has appointed is troubled by the idle, indeed broken, which is great sin and wickedness.

but are busybodies: He reprehends a vice, which is joined with the former, upon which follows an infinite sort of mischiefs: that is, that there are none more busy in other men's matters, than they who neglect their own.

Now them that are such we: The Lord commands and the apostles pray in the name of Christ, first, that no man be idle, and next, that every man quietly and carefully sees to do his duty in that office and calling in which the Lord has placed him.
But ye: We must take heed that the unworthiness of some men does not cause us to be slack in well-doing.
And if any man obey not: Excommunication is a punishment for the obstinate.
company with him: We must have no familiarity or fellowship with the one who has been excommunicated.
that he may be ashamed: The end of the excommunication is not the destruction, but the salvation of the sinner, that at least through shame he may be driven to repentance.

Yet count him not as an: We must avoid familiarity with the one who has been excommunicated in such a way, that we diligently seek every occasion and means that may be, to bring them again into the right way.
Now the Lord of peace himself: Prayers are the seals of all exhortations.
The salutation of Paul with mine: The apostle writes the conclusion of his letter with his own hand, so that false letters might not be brought and put in place of true ones.
